The North Quays main contract works programme is signifi cantly 
advanced and progressing well.  The substructure works for the 
Sustainable Transport Bridge is continuing, the fi rst of four piers is 
now visible within the most southerly cofferdamThe fabrication of the 
steel deck superstructure in Belgium is c. 75% complete. The pile 
support slab for the South Plaza is substantially complete.  
The Transport Hub building concourse and the support walls for 
the station concourse and columns are substantially complete, with 
works continuing on the station platforms.  Works have also 
progressed to installing the bridge/ concourse precast beams and 
external lift shafts.   
Road and access infrastructure is progressing well, with works 
continuing on the various bridge structures, in particular with 
western access bridge and greenway underpasses.Traffi c 
management measures continue to be in place, with works 
continuing along the median at Dock Road / Fountain Street.

Economic Development & Enterprise SPC
The next Economic Development & Enterprise SPC will be held in October 2024.  
New York Times Article: VW commissioned the creation of a video showcasing the recent awards and accolades, 
including Waterford featuring in the New York Times Top 52 places to go in 2024, won by the county. This video was 
sent to all VW members for them to use and issued to the media with a press release promoting the Best of Waterford 
experience. As a result, VW was featured in Hospitality News, Dining in Dublin and by Pòl O Conghalie on The Today 
Show. 
Winter Ad Campaign: Jan – March
Paid ads included 2 social uplift features on the Irish Independent with a guaranteed reach of 160,000 per video. The 
fi rst video showcased the tourism offering in Waterford City and brought audiences to the Best of Waterford experience 
on the Visit Waterford Website. The second showcased the county and brought visitors to the explore page on the VW 
website. VW also ran a print ad in the Irish Independent Spring Supplement. A further digital ad will be released on 
March 24th. Visit Waterford also had radio ads running on Beat and Today FM. Visit Waterford are currently running a 
competition on Lorcan Murray’s Classic Drive for a 2 night stay, B&B and dinner on one evening at The Tower Hotel.
Portia Jones-Travel Goals Podcast
VW worked with Fáilte Ireland and Tourism Ireland to welcome Portia Jones to Waterford, Portia visited a number of VW 
members during her visit including, Waterford Treasures, Sólás na Mara, Waterford Distillery and Mount Congreve 
Gardens. She produced a 2 part podcast as a result of her visit. VW have established a working group to facilitate a 
coordinated welcome for cruise ships to Waterford, ensuring passengers can experience as much of Waterford as 
possible during their visit. The group includes representatives from VW, WCCC, Port of Waterford, Bus Eireann, 
Excursions Ireland, Volunteer Waterford and the Harbour Master in Dunmore East. Actions have been agreed and the 
group are working together to deliver clear communications and transport options to passengers as well as ensuring 
they have a warm welcome through the Waterford Ambassador Programme.
Waterford’s St. Patrick’s Day Festival 2024 
VW worked with WCCC to promote the four day St. Patrick’s Day Festival in Waterford City. As part of the promotional 
activities VW ran a number of international ad campaigns across digital platforms reaching approx. 162,000 people 
across North America, UK, France and Germany. The domestic campaign included digital ads, competitions and a press 
release. As a result of the press release The St. Patrick’s Day Festival was featured in a number of regional and national 
publications, including Irish Country Magazine, The Irish Star and Waterford Live.

Management Report Plenary 13th October 2022
The Derelict Sites Team are currently dealing with 280 properties that are considered either derelict or potentially 
derelict.  The activity in recent weeks has substantially increased with 82 derelict on the Derelict Sites Register.  Initial 
engagement with owners or their representatives is key to resolution of the issues of dereliction and to understand the 
various reasons why the properties are in a derelict stage.  To date we have 280 Derelict Site fi les open. 
The level of activity in the property market for vacant and derelict properties has increased and of the properties we 
have identifi ed as derelict, several of them have been brought to the market and some are at ‘to let’/ ‘sale agreed’ stage. 
We continue the engagement with the new owners of those properties to ensure they are aware of their responsibilities 
under the Derelict Sites Act, 1990.  Due to the Vacant Property refurbishment Grant, there is a noticeable increase in the 
number of derelict and vacant properties on the market at the current time..

COMPULSORY PURCHASE ACQUISITION OF DERELICT SITES (CPA)
There were 2 CPA’s initiated in March and publicly advertised.  The deadline for submissions expires at the start of April. 
The Council will move to the vesting process where applications for registration of title will be made to the Property 
Registration Authority.  In April, we are commencing work on three further CPAs.
DERELICT SITE LEVY 
Determination of valuations on the derelict sites which are on the Derelict Sites Register has commenced and notices 
have issued to 58 property owners. Eight properties have appealed the valuation to the Valuation Tribunal and a 
decision is awaited. The levy is an annual levy while the property remains on the Derelict Sites Register and amounts to 
7% of the value of the property, on an annual basis. This will be further progressed in 2024.

Heritage Officer Report 
Decade of Commemorations
Waterford’s Two Civil wars- Armed conflict and national strife in Waterford 1922-1924 a publication by Dr. Pat McCarthy 
will take place on Wednesday April 3rd in the Garden Room of Waterford Medieval Museum. The book was funded 
through the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sports and Media’s Decade of Commemorations Fund.  
The Department have allocated €15,000 for the 2024 Commemorations Fund which will be allocated to support of film 
and publications and a programme celebrating the Irish language in the development of the Free State in 1924.
Heritage Plan Grant Scheme
All four projects submitted to the Heritage Council’s Heritage Plan Fund have been successful and funding has been 
allocated. 
Community Heritage Grant Scheme 2024
Over 10 applications have been submitted from community groups across the county for the Heritage Council’s 
Community Heritage Grant Scheme.  The fund is open to   community/voluntary and not-for-profit organisations for 
heritage projects which must be completed by 15th of November 2024. Last year, seven Waterford-based projects were 
funded through the scheme. 
Community Monuments Scheme
Six applications have been submitted from projects across the City and County under the Community Monuments 
Scheme 2024 which provides funding for the conservation and interpretation of archaeological sites and monuments 
pre-1700. The outcome of the application process will be known by end of April.
Conservation Officer
Waterford receives €506,693 in funding for Built Heritage  
Malcolm Noonan TD, Minister of State for Heritage and Electoral Reform at the Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage has announced funding under 2 schemes for Protected Structures and historic buildings - the 
Built Heritage Investment Scheme (BHIS) 2024 and the Historic Structures Fund (HSF) 2024. 
In Waterford, funding of €242,400 will be provided for 27 projects for private and public buildings in the city and county 
under the BHIS scheme. This will support works such as   the repair of historic roofs, walls and chimneys, repair of 
joinery and repair of historic stained glass. This funding also includes €73,793 which has been ring- fenced specifically 
for thatch house projects.  
Under the Historic Structure Fund €264,000 has been allocated for 4 projects.

COMMUNITY GRANTS
Waterford City and County Council (WCCC), at its plenary meeting on 14th March 2024, approved 288 allocations under 
the Supporting Waterford Communities Fund 2024. The scheme provides grant aid assistance to community groups, 
residents associations and sports clubs who are engaged in community activity, providing community services or carrying 
out improvement works. The total fund for 2024 was €241,430. Waterford LCDC, at at its meeting on 14th March 2024,
 approved 164 allocations under the Local Enhancrment  Programme (LEP) 2024 General Fund (total fund of €153,405.12) 
and a further 26 allocations under the ring fenced Women’s Fund (total fund €31,824.28).  
The LEP is funded by the Department of Rural and Community Development and administered by Waterford LCDC / 
WCCC. It’s aimed at supporting groups, particularly in disadvantaged areas, with minor capital works and improvements 
to their facilities, and the purchase of equipment for community use.  The Community Recognition Fund 2024 was 
launchted by Minister Heather Mumphreys on the 15th March.Once finalised, details of the fund will be included on the 
Council’s website and communicated via the PPN and the Council’s social media fora.

General Update 
Healthy Waterford, a leading organization in promoting wellness within the community of Waterford, has undoubtedly 
made remarkable progress in the past year. Thanks to its dedicated efforts and unwavering commitment, we have wit-
nessed significant improvements in the community sector, especially within the Waterford City and County Council. One 
of the key objectives of Healthy Waterford has been to fulfil its targets set by the Department of Health. 
One of the most noteworthy achievements of Healthy Waterford in the current year has been the successful execution of 
Connecting Community Roadshows within the Municipal District Model of Wellbeing with the PPN. These roadshows have 
not only created awareness about the importance of health and wellness in the community, but they have also brought 
people together and fostered a sense of unity and solidarity among them.  But Healthy Waterford does not intend to stop 
there.  It has already scheduled Connecting Community Roadshows on an ongoing basis and are working on inclusion 
on Municipal District meetings on an annual basis, ensuring that the message of health and wellness reaches every nook 
and corner of the community. This proactive approach towards promoting and encouraging a healthier lifestyle is truly 
commendable and deserves recognition.  
The second consecutive launch of the much-awaited ‘Playful Streets’ initiative by Healthy Waterford has been a mas-
sive success. This program aims to transform the streets into safe and playful areas for children to engage in physical 
activities, promoting a more active lifestyle. This year, the number of expressions of interest received for ‘Playful Streets’ 
has surpassed all expectations, with over 40 enthusiastic communities signing up. This not only indicates the increasing 
popularity of the program but also showcases the growing awareness among the community regarding the importance of 
physical activity for overall health and well-being. It is evident that Healthy Waterford has emerged as a pioneer in promot-
ing and advocating for a healthier and happier community. It’s efforts and initiatives have not only improved the physical 
health of individuals but have also positively impacted their mental and emotional well-being. 
 
KEY PROJECT SPOTLIGHT – SOCIAL FARMING  
Thanks to a robust collaboration among stakeholders, the council and these groups have successfully formed positive 
relationships.  8 Social Farming Placements took place, one day a week, for 12 weeks. 9 participants took part in the 
placements and 100 Social Farming days were delivered. Social Farming provides outcome focused placements for 
people accessing support services. The participants that attended the farms as part of this funding came from Intellectual 
Disability services. This enables the participants do normal everyday activities that we all do. The participants also helped 
out prepare for a local event which gave them the opportunity to work with local people which they may not have met 
otherwise. It is all the time integrating people with ID in our community. 
NEW INITIATIVE – MINDING YOUR MENTAL HEALTH MESSAGING FOR WATERFORD GAA CLUBS 
Initiated in partnership with the HSE Connecting for Life Team in South East Community Healthcare, the signage high-
lights ways that you can mind your mental health and promotes the services available if you need to access support. 
The signage was developed in collaboration with Healthy Waterford/WCCC, Mental Health Ireland and the Waterford 
GAA Health and Wellbeing Committee.  52 signs will be delivered to GAA clubs and a launch took place recently. It is the 
intention of the Waterford GAA health and Wellbeing committee, supported by Healthy Waterford, to continue this action 
throughout 2024 and embed the signage initiative.        
NEW INITIATIVE – GROW IT FORWARD 
Over 450 packs of food growing equipment were distributed. This has over 2000 packets that will support local 
communities to grow their own food. This will entail a 12-week programme of education. GROW it Forward is a 
food education & sustainability programme designed to educate, inspire and empower individuals to grow, 
share and understand how their local action can deliver global impact. GIY & Healthy Waterford will undertake pre and 
post programme evaluation to understand the Food Empathy impact of GROW it Forward. Food Empathy are the changes 
in knowledge, behaviour and attitude that happens when people start to grow some of their own food.

UKRAINIAN COMMUNITY RESPONSE FORUM:
The Ukrainian CRF is in place to assist with housing, supporting and integrating Ukrainian refugees into our communities. 
All key agencies are working in collaboration to provide services and supports to all Ukrainians arriving into Waterford.  
To date over 105,500 (@ 24th March) temporary protections have been granted to Ukrainians arriving to Ireland, with in 
excess of 2,904 of those registered here in Waterford. Waterford City & County Council have provided temporary 
accommodation directly to over 2,110 Ukrainian refugees in the Council run rest centres and have matched over 1,586 of 
those with pledged and Council sourced accommodation. Over 760 Ukrainians are accommodated in pledged properties 
throughout Waterford currently with new pledges required on an ongoing basis.    Any queries on same should be directed 
to offerahome@waterfordcouncil.ie or 058 22059

ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION & AWARENESS
Green-Schools promotes long-term, whole-school action for the environment Green-Schools with primary and secondary 
schools. There are 61 schools in Co. Waterford due to renew their Green Flag this year. A renewal visit must take place 
before a school submits a renewal application form for their renewal Green Flags (Energy, Water, Travel, Biodiversity and 
the Global Citizenship themes). Renewal visits are carried out by the Environment Awareness Officer. The purpose of the 
visit is to demonstrate that the school has an active Green-Schools programme in operation and has been maintaining 
previous themes in addition to working on the current theme. Schools applying must first complete an assessment visit 
from the Environment Awareness Officer before submitting their renewal application. All Green Schools working on a flag 
for this current school year must receive a visit and submit an application by 15th March. Themes range from Litter & 
Waste to Water and Biodiversity. This has meant lots of school visits have been taking place recently to meet with Green 
School Committees and talks to classes.
COMMUNITY CLEAN-UPS
Waterford City & County Council facilitates community clean ups throughout the year to clean up litter and illegally 
dumped waste from approach roads, local beauty spots, beaches and general public areas. The Environment Department 
continue to supply bags, gloves and litter pickers to many of the groups taking part, distributing them from both our 
Dungarvan and Waterford offices. Collection of any bags of litter is then organised for after the clean-up takes place. 
National Spring Clean takes place throughout the month of April. Registrations are now being taken at 
www.nationalspringclean.org As part of this the Environment Department supply bags, gloves and litter pickers to many 
of the groups taking part, as well as collecting the bags of  litter for all clean ups. Groups are encouraged to register their 
clean up as a National Spring Clean event to receive additional resources from An Taisce.

Connecting Communities Roadshow 
The Environment Department is taking part in a Connecting Communities Roadshow at 7 locations around the county 
this spring. Currently, other partners at the Roadshow include various WCCC departments, Waterford PPN, Waterford 
Sports Partnership, Waterford Leader, Waterford Area Partnership, Local Link. HSE Health Promotion, Waterford Volun-
teer Centre, Community Guards, Fire Service and WWETB, with the idea that the greater the collaboration, the better the 
attendance at each roadshow. Environment’s display will focus on waste prevention. 
Rubbish Schools Film Festival
The Environment Department is working with Createschool to offer 5 secondary schools in County Waterford the opportu-
nity to participate the Rubbish Film. The Rubbish Film Festival is a really unique opportunity for Transition Year Students 
to showcase their creative talents, create awareness on Environmental Issues such as Climate Action and learn some 
new digital storytelling skills in the process. Each participating school will receive an intensive 2-day workshop on-site in 
their school from Createschool to help them gain and/or develop the skills to create their own short ONE MINUTE film 
or films that will create awareness among their peers on their selected environmental issue. All costs are covered by the 
Environment Section of Waterford City & County Council. An awards ceremony will take place in late April for this
